title: Information-Guided Selective Modality-Interest Alignment for Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2608.27950v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal recommendation (MMRec) aims to enhance recommendation performance by leveraging rich item content from multiple modalities. However, directly incorporating all modality information does not necessarily lead to better preference modeling, since user interests are often more related to a subset of modality signals, while other signals may be weakly aligned with user preferences or even introduce noise. Although recent MMRec methods improve modality utilization through invariant learning, attention mechanisms, graph refinement, or contrastive learning, their alignment processes are often implicit or heuristic and lack a clear objective for selecting modality signals that better match user interests.   In this paper, we propose AMUR, an information-guided selective modality-interest alignment framework for multimodal recommendation. translated_title: 面向多模态推荐的信息引导式选择性模态-兴趣对齐
translated_abstract: 多模态推荐旨在通过利用来自多种模态的丰富物品内容来提升推荐性能。然而，直接引入所有模态信息并不一定能带来更好的偏好建模，因为用户兴趣往往仅与一部分模态信号更相关，而其他信号可能与用户偏好关联较弱，甚至引入噪声。尽管近期的多模态推荐方法通过不变学习、注意力机制、图精炼或对比学习等方式改进了模态利用，但它们的对齐过程通常是隐式的或启发式的，缺乏一个明确的目标来筛选更能匹配用户兴趣的模态信号。在本文中，我们提出了AMUR，一个面向多模态推荐的信息引导式选择性模态-兴趣对齐框架。受信息论视角的启发，AMUR旨在增强与用户兴趣更相关的模态信息（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出AMUR框架，从信息论视角出发，通过信息引导的选择性模态-兴趣对齐机制，筛选并增强与用户兴趣更相关的模态信号，避免无关或噪声模态信息的干扰，从而提升多模态推荐的性能。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes AMUR, an information-guided selective modality-interest alignment framework that, from an information-theoretic perspective, selects and enhances modality signals most relevant to user interests while filtering out weakly aligned or noisy ones, thereby improving multimodal recommendation performance.
